title: Disc or hoop: which rolls down first?
hook: Same mass, same size, same ramp. A solid disc and a thin hoop roll down. Who wins?

knows: a heavier object is pulled down harder
doesNotKnow: that a rolling object's energy is shared between moving along and spinning
that mass far from the axis takes a bigger share for spinning

misconception: Objects of the same mass and size roll down at the same speed, or the heavier one wins.
objective: The learner can explain that a hoop, with all its mass at the rim, puts more of its energy into spinning than a solid disc, so it gains speed more slowly and loses the race whatever its mass.

claims.text: Rolling without slipping down a slope, an object's acceleration is g sin(angle) / (1 + I / (m r²)): 1/2 for a solid disc, 1 for a thin hoop, whatever the mass or radius.
claims.source: Newton's second law for translation and rotation with the rolling condition a = alpha r: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 11.1 Rolling Motion (Example 11.1). I/(m r^2) = 1/2 for a solid cylinder or disc, 1 for a thin hoop (section 10.5, Figure 10.20).

claims.text: On a 30° ramp the disc accelerates at 3.27 m/s² and the hoop at 2.45 m/s²; down 2 m from rest the disc takes 1.11 s and the hoop 1.28 s.
Doubling the hoop's mass does not change its time: mass cancels out of the acceleration.
claims.source: Follows from c1: the acceleration contains only g, the angle and I/(m r^2), a shape factor.

claims.text: A rolling object's energy is shared between moving along and spinning; a hoop puts half of it into spinning, a solid disc a third (33%).
claims.source: KE = 1/2 m v^2 (1 + I/(m r^2)); spin share = k / (1 + k): hoop 1/2, disc (1/2)/(3/2) = 1/3. OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 11.1. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): Spin share = k/(1+k) with I = k m r^2: hoop k=1 gives 1/2, solid disc k=1/2 gives 1/3 (OpenStax University Physics 1, 11.1). Reveal matches.

claims.text: Idealisations: rolling without slipping and no air drag or rolling resistance; the race is shown in slow motion.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('No slipping, no air drag', clock marked slow-mo; animation at 1/3 real speed).

recall.question: A heavy steel ring and a light wooden disc of the same radius roll down the same slope from rest. Which reaches the bottom first?
recall.why: Mass cancels; only shape counts. The ring has all its mass at the rim, so more of its energy goes into spinning and less into speed.
